title: Restriction map bijectivity assuming finite fibre
statement:
theorem finite_pushforward_set_stalk_map_bijective_of_finite
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    (H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y)
    (hfin : Finite {x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X // x ≫ f = y}) :
    Function.Bijective
        (fun a : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber.obj
            ((f.Etale.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
              Y.smallEtaleTopology X.smallEtaleTopology).obj H) ↦
          fun t : {x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X // x ≫ f = y} ↦
            (colimit.pre
              ((CategoryOfElements.π (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber).op ⋙ H.obj)
              (Etale.baseChangeNbhd f y t).op) a)

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero) (1), first display (for F in Sh(X_etale)), and its proof (X x_Y Spec O^sh_{Y,ybar} is a finite disjoint union of spectra of strictly henselian local rings, one for each point over ybar; sections over it are the product of the stalks by Lemma Tag 03QO, which is stated for sheaves of sets); the map, implicit in Stacks, is the restriction of germs; sets version of lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction

proof.text: Compute the pushforward stalk on the opposite of the cofiltered split-neighbourhood category: the forgetful functor is initial, so its opposite is final. Functor.Final.colimitIso gives e₀.
Compute each fibre stalk using the initial t-th-piece functor, obtaining e₁ t by Functor.Final.colimitIso.
The section functor on split neighbourhoods is naturally the product of its piece-section functors, through restrictions to each piece.

Use hfin to choose a Fintype for the geometric fibre. Filtered colimits of Type-valued functors preserve finite limits, hence this product; apply PreservesProduct.iso to the piece-section functors. This holds also for an empty fibre.

Check the composite on each colimit coprojection and each product projection. The piece inclusion is a morphism of pointed neighbourhoods, so colimit.w identifies the restricted piece germ with the base-change neighbourhood germ. Thus e₀.hom followed by Pi.lift r equals the composite of the section-product, colimit-product, and piece-stalk isomorphisms. Pi.lift r is therefore an isomorphism. Compose with Types.productIso; its projections show its underlying function is precisely the map in the statement, and hence bijective.

proof_origin.place: H2 adapts the split-neighbourhood proof of stalkIsoColimitSections_hom_comp_piLift_stalkRestrict to Type coefficients using Mathlib filtered_colim_preservesFiniteLimits_of_types
